domain_label: Oven Spring, Doming & Doneness (cupcake bake subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is oven spring, doming, structural set, and doneness of cupcakes, finer than a whole-baking KB
doneness targets a set crumb at roughly 98-100C internal unless a recipe overrides the endpoint
a mixed cupcake batter is already portioned into lined cavities; mixing and formulation chemistry are upstream
exclusions: ingredient sourcing, mixing method, and creaming/emulsion build
staling, storage, and shelf-life chemistry beyond pull-point moisture
commercial tunnel-oven engineering and energy optimization
allergen labeling and sanitation procedures beyond the doneness safety floor

competency_questions.question: What batter viscosity holds gas for a dome without running flat?
What fill level balances dome height against overflow?
How is oven spring driven and sustained until the structure sets?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OVEN_SPRING and LEAVEN_TIMING describe gas timing

competency_questions.question: How do starch gelatinization and protein coagulation set the crumb?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STARCH_GEL and PROTEIN_SET define the set points

competency_questions.question: How is doneness confirmed by temperature, springback, and toothpick?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DONE_INTERNAL_TEMP, DONE_SPRINGBACK, DONE_TOOTHPICK each define a test

competency_questions.question: What are the root causes and preventions for sinking, overflow, peaking, and cracking?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: defect nodes enumerate causes and fixes

competency_questions.question: How do fill and viscosity jointly govern doming?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FILL_LEVEL and BATTER_VISCOSITY interact for dome control

competency_questions.question: How is carryover used to set the pull point without drying the crumb?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CARRYOVER defines pull point and carryover estimate

competency_questions.question: What internal temperature confirms a cupcake is set?
How are oven temperature, preheat, rack, and convection controlled for even rise?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: oven-control nodes specify calibration and placement

competency_questions.question: What doneness floor keeps egg and dairy batter safe?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FOOD_SAFETY_DONE sets a safe internal temperature floor

competency_questions.question: When does food safety override a texture preference for underbaking?

glossary.definition: the rapid early rise of batter from thermal gas expansion, steam, and leavener release before the crumb sets
the rounded raised top formed when rise outpaces and then is locked by structural set
the heat-driven swelling and setting of starch granules in available water, roughly 60-90C, that sets the crumb
heat denaturation of egg and flour proteins into a set network forming crumb walls
the state where starch is set, proteins coagulated, and free water reduced so the crumb is cooked through
residual heat that continues cooking the center after the cupcake leaves the oven
the recovery of a cupcake top to its shape after a light press, signaling surface set
a tall narrow pointed top from a fast rise set against an early-set rim
the temperature range where microbes proliferate in egg/dairy batter, to be passed through to a safe set temperature

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for cupcake oven-spring, doming, set, and doneness work units in absence of supplied datasets
grounding_limits: domain-general heuristic priors grounded in standard baking-science references

nodes.definition: Tune batter viscosity (sugar, liquid, mixing) so trapped gas can expand into a dome without bubbles collapsing or batter running flat.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: crumb collapses or tops run flat across a batch

pros.claim: Viscosity that holds gas yet flows lets the dome form and set in place
pros.example: thick-but-pourable batter mounds then sets

cons.claim: Too thin runs flat and overflows; too thick traps no rise
cons.example: watery batter spreads and bakes flat

failure_modes: batter too thin from excess sugar/liquid
acceptance_tests: batch tops dome rather than spread
revisit_triggers: new flour or sugar lot alters flow

nodes.definition: Choose fill level (about two-thirds) to balance dome height against overflow and muffin-top spread.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: overflow or sunken centers recur at chosen fill

pros.claim: Two-thirds fill leaves headroom for spring while still doming
pros.example: 2/3 fill domes above the rim cleanly

cons.claim: Overfilling overflows and creates dense gummy muffin-tops
cons.example: filled to rim batter spills and bakes flat-edged

acceptance_tests: fill fraction within target band by weight

nodes.definition: Manage the initial burst of rise from gas expansion, steam, and leavener release before the structure sets.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: rise stalls or collapses before set

pros.claim: Coordinated gas expansion and steam lift the crumb before gelatinization locks it
pros.example: CO2 plus steam expands cells then starch sets them

cons.claim: Spring spent before the structure can hold it collapses the center
cons.example: gas peaks early then batter falls

acceptance_tests: measured rise occurs in first third of bake

nodes.definition: Match single vs double-acting leavener release to the bake so gas peaks while batter can still expand and then sets.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: peaked or hollow tops trace to early gas

pros.claim: Double-acting release in oven heat sustains lift until set
pros.example: second gas burst at oven heat holds the dome

cons.claim: All gas released at mix time leaves nothing for oven spring
cons.example: over-rested batter goes flat

failure_modes: gas spent during long bench rest
acceptance_tests: batter baked within leavener active window
no flat tops from spent gas

nodes.definition: Drive starch gelatinization (roughly 60-90C) to convert flowing batter into a set crumb that locks the risen shape.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: centers gummy or set too early flattening dome

pros.claim: Gelatinized starch sets the expanded foam into a stable crumb
pros.example: starch swells and sets locking risen cells

cons.claim: Incomplete gelatinization leaves a gummy raw-tasting center
cons.example: underbaked center stays wet and dense

failure_modes: premature set capping the dome low

nodes.definition: Coagulate egg and flour proteins at their set point to co-build crumb walls without overcoagulating into rubber.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: crumb rubbery or fails to hold structure

pros.claim: Coagulated proteins build crumb walls that hold the gas foam
pros.example: egg proteins set into a springy network

cons.claim: Overcoagulation makes a tough rubbery crumb
cons.example: overbaked egg-rich batter turns rubbery

acceptance_tests: crumb walls set without rubbery toughness

nodes.definition: Confirm doneness by probing internal temperature to about 98-100C, the most reliable signal that starch set and free water boiled off.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: temp passes but crumb still raw or vice versa

pros.claim: Internal temp near 98-100C objectively confirms the set without cutting
pros.example: probe reads 99C and center is set

cons.claim: A miscalibrated probe or bad placement gives a false done call
cons.example: probe in air pocket reads low and misleads

failure_modes: false done from probe in air pocket
undercooked center passing a glance test
acceptance_tests: probe placement avoids pan and pockets

nodes.definition: Use the gentle press springback test as a fast non-destructive doneness check that the surface set and resists indentation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: springback passes but center underbaked

pros.claim: Springback gives an instant non-destructive read of surface set
pros.example: top springs back fully signaling set

cons.claim: Surface set can mask a still-wet center on deep batters
cons.example: springy top over a raw core

acceptance_tests: top recovers fully from a light press

nodes.definition: Apply the toothpick/skewer test to read crumb moisture at the center, distinguishing wet batter from a few moist crumbs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: pick clean yet temp shows underdone or overdone

pros.claim: Toothpick reads center moisture cheaply and quickly
pros.example: pick out with moist crumbs not wet batter

cons.claim: Reading clean too strictly overbakes and dries the crumb
cons.example: waiting for bone-dry pick dries cupcakes

failure_modes: misreading melted sugar as wet batter
acceptance_tests: pick emerges with moist crumbs not raw batter

nodes.definition: Pull cupcakes slightly before full set so carryover (residual heat) finishes the bake without drying the crumb.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: crumb dries on cooling despite correct pull temp

pros.claim: Carryover finishes set so the crumb stays moist not dried
pros.example: pulled at 96C it coasts to set while cooling

cons.claim: Ignoring carryover overbakes and dries every batch
cons.example: baked to fully dry then dries further on rack

failure_modes: pulling far too early leaving raw center
acceptance_tests: pull point accounts for measured carryover rise
cooled crumb is moist and set

nodes.definition: Diagnose and prevent overflow where batter spills over the liner, caused by overfill, over-leavening, or too-thin batter.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: overflow recurs after fill correction

pros.claim: Capping fill and leavener stops batter spilling and burning on the pan
pros.example: 2/3 fill and balanced soda end overflow

cons.claim: Chasing tall domes by overfilling guarantees spillover
cons.example: filled high to dome it overflows instead

acceptance_tests: batches bake within the liner without spill

nodes.definition: Diagnose and prevent sunken centers from underbaking, over-leavening, excess sugar/liquid, or oven-door shock.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: centers keep sinking after corrections

pros.claim: Setting the structure before gas exhausts prevents the center falling
pros.example: crumb sets before gas peak passes

cons.claim: Over-leavening or opening the door early collapses the rise
cons.example: early door peek drops the half-set center

acceptance_tests: no collapse from leavener or door events
revisit_triggers: oven seal or door habit change

nodes.definition: Prevent excessive peaking (volcano tops) from oven too hot, batter too thick, or over-leavening forcing a fast narrow rise.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: peaks persist after temperature drop

pros.claim: Moderating heat and thinning batter spreads the rise into a round dome
pros.example: lower temp turns a peak into a dome

cons.claim: Hot oven sets the rim fast forcing batter up a narrow center
cons.example: crust sets early then center erupts upward

failure_modes: oven too hot setting rim early
batter too thick forcing narrow rise
acceptance_tests: tops dome roundly without sharp peaks

nodes.definition: Prevent surface cracking from a too-hot oven or fast crust set that splits as interior gas keeps expanding.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cracks persist after temperature reduction

pros.claim: A slower crust set lets the surface stretch with interior expansion
pros.example: lower heat lets the top stretch not split

cons.claim: A flash-set crust splits as gas keeps pushing underneath
cons.example: hot top sets then cracks as center rises

acceptance_tests: crust sets in pace with rise

nodes.definition: Verify true oven temperature and hot/cold zones with an independent thermometer so the bake profile matches the recipe.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake outcomes drift across same recipe and time

pros.claim: A verified true temperature makes spring, set, and doneness reproducible
pros.example: thermometer reveals a 15C dial offset to correct

cons.claim: An uncalibrated oven silently causes peaking, sinking, or raw centers
cons.example: dial says 175C but cavity runs 160C

acceptance_tests: measured cavity temp within tolerance of target
zone map documented for rack choice

nodes.definition: Fully preheat and protect thermal mass so initial heat drives oven spring and door openings do not stall the rise.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: weak spring traces to under-preheat or temp drop

pros.claim: Full preheat delivers the heat burst that drives early oven spring
pros.example: soaked oven hits batter with full spring heat

cons.claim: Loading a cold or freshly-opened oven starves the spring
cons.example: cold-start bake yields a weak flat rise

failure_modes: temperature crash from prolonged door opening
acceptance_tests: oven soaked at target before loading

nodes.definition: Place pans on the rack that balances bottom and top heat so domes rise evenly without burnt bottoms or pale set tops.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: uneven doming or burnt bottoms recur

pros.claim: Center rack balances radiant bottom and top heat for even domes
pros.example: center rack gives even rise and color

cons.claim: Too low burns bottoms before the top sets and domes
cons.example: bottom-rack bake scorches base, pale top

acceptance_tests: domes rise evenly across the pan
no scorched bottoms or pale set tops

nodes.definition: Decide convection vs static and adjust temperature so forced air speeds set without skewing domes or drying tops.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: convection skews domes or dries tops

pros.claim: Convection with a temperature drop sets faster and more evenly
pros.example: fan plus 15C lower bakes even and quick

cons.claim: Full-temp convection sets crust too fast and lopsides domes
cons.example: fan at recipe temp dries and tilts tops

acceptance_tests: mode and temperature chosen for even set

nodes.definition: Enforce a non-negotiable doneness floor so egg and dairy batter reaches a safe internal temperature, overriding any texture preference for underbaking.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any undercooked egg/dairy batter reaches consumers

pros.claim: A safety floor guarantees egg/dairy batter is cooked through regardless of texture goals
pros.example: center hits safe set temp before any underbake preference

cons.claim: Underbaking for gooeyness risks foodborne illness from raw egg/dairy
cons.example: molten center left raw endangers eaters

failure_modes: batter held in temperature danger zone
acceptance_tests: center reaches and holds safe internal temperature

nodes.definition: Trade residual moistness against full structural set, choosing a bake endpoint that keeps the crumb moist yet stable enough to hold the dome.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: crumb either gummy or dry at chosen endpoint

pros.claim: A tuned endpoint keeps the crumb moist while still fully set and stable
pros.example: pull at full set yet just-moist crumb

cons.claim: Pushing moistness too far leaves a gummy under-set crumb that collapses
cons.example: stopping early for moisture gives a wet sinking center

acceptance_tests: crumb is moist and holds structure after cooling

edges.example: egg set firms the crumb walls

edges.why_related: starch and protein set co-build the crumb

edges.why_related: both confirm doneness by different signals

edges.why_related: both confirm doneness redundantly

over-leavening collapses the center

edges.resolution_rule: food safety floor dominates; never underbake egg/dairy below the safe set temperature for moisture

edges.why_related: moisture goal pulls against full gelatinization
edges.example: under-set for moisture gives gummy crumb
edges.resolution_rule: require complete gelatinization first, then maximize residual moisture within set

edges.why_related: carryover is the lever to keep moisture while finishing set
edges.example: pull early and let carryover finish

edges.why_related: high fill for tall domes pushes toward peaking and overflow
edges.example: filling high for height peaks and spills
edges.resolution_rule: cap fill at the dome band; gain height via spring not overfill

edges.why_related: a bone-dry pick target conflicts with a moist endpoint

conflict_axes.trigger: pulling early for moisture leaves the crumb under-set and prone to collapse
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if the crumb is not fully gelatinized, structural set dominates and the bake continues
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: center below set temp at pull
conflict_axes.example: stopping at 90C for moisture yields a gummy sinking center

conflict_axes.trigger: more sugar/fat for tenderness thins and weakens the structure that supports the dome
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if tops run flat, rise-supporting viscosity dominates over added tenderness
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: flat or sunken tops across a batch
conflict_axes.example: extra sugar tenderizes but flattens the dome

conflict_axes.trigger: filling higher for a taller dome increases overflow and muffin-top spread
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if overflow occurs, the fill cap dominates over the height goal
conflict_axes.example: filling to the rim for height spills over the liner

conflict_axes.trigger: raising temperature to bake faster flash-sets the crust and causes peaks and cracks
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if peaks or cracks appear, even-set quality dominates over speed
conflict_axes.example: a hot fast oven peaks and cracks tops

conflict_axes.trigger: baking until a bone-dry pick over-bakes and dries the crumb
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: once internal temp confirms set, moisture preservation dominates over a drier visual test
conflict_axes.example: chasing a dry toothpick dries the cupcake

conflict_axes.trigger: a preference for a gooey underbaked center risks raw egg and dairy
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: food safety dominates absolutely; egg/dairy batter must reach the safe set temperature regardless of texture goals
conflict_axes.example: a molten center left raw to taste fudgy is unsafe

conflict_axes.trigger: setting too early caps the dome low while setting too late lets the risen foam collapse
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if the dome collapses, set timing dominates and must capture peak height
conflict_axes.example: early set traps a low rise; late set lets it fall

conflict_axes.trigger: skipping full preheat or crowding pans to save time weakens spring and evenness
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if spring or evenness suffers, bake quality dominates over time saved
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: weak or uneven rise from rushing
conflict_axes.example: loading a cold oven to save time flattens the rise

conflict_axes.trigger: a wetter fresh crumb stales and turns gummy faster than a fully set crumb
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if shelf stability matters, full set dominates over maximal fresh moisture
conflict_axes.example: an under-set moist crumb sours and turns gummy quickly

edge_cases.example: probe in a large cell reads 88C in a set cupcake

edge_cases.detection_method: log door events against rise stage

edge_cases.trigger: cavities filled above the dome band
edge_cases.failure_mode: batter overflows and bakes onto the pan
edge_cases.example: filled to the rim then spills over the liner

edge_cases.trigger: batter rests too long before baking
edge_cases.failure_mode: gas spent before oven heat yields flat rise
edge_cases.example: single-acting batter rested an hour bakes flat

edge_cases.failure_mode: wet gummy center under a set-looking top
edge_cases.example: springy top hides a raw 90C core

edge_cases.trigger: egg/dairy center left below the safe set temperature
edge_cases.example: a deliberately gooey center stays under the safe temperature

edge_cases.trigger: oven runs hotter than the dial indicates
edge_cases.failure_mode: rim sets early forcing a volcano peak
edge_cases.detection_method: thermometer check plus top shape audit

edge_cases.trigger: crust flash-sets while interior still expands
edge_cases.example: a hot top cracks as the center keeps rising

edge_cases.trigger: baked to full dryness ignoring carryover
edge_cases.example: baked bone-dry then dries further while cooling
edge_cases.detection_method: compare pull temp to final crumb moisture

edge_cases.trigger: trusting the dial across a hot/cold zone
edge_cases.example: front cavities pale while back ones scorch

edge_cases.failure_mode: gas escapes and tops bake flat
edge_cases.example: a runny batter spreads and never domes

edge_cases.trigger: high airflow with no temperature drop
edge_cases.example: fan tilts and dries the tops on one side
edge_cases.detection_method: compare dome symmetry across the pan

workflow.objective: verify true temperature, map zones, and fully preheat
workflow.do_first_because: every rise and set outcome depends on true oven temperature

workflow.objective: set viscosity for rise and fill cavities to the dome band
workflow.do_first_because: viscosity and fill govern doming before any heat is applied

workflow.objective: bake within the leavener active window for sustained spring
workflow.do_first_because: spent gas before bake cannot be recovered in the oven

workflow.objective: drive and sustain the initial rise until structure can hold it
acceptance_tests: rise occurs in first third of bake
workflow.do_first_because: spring must complete before the crumb sets

workflow.objective: complete gelatinization and coagulation to lock the dome
workflow.do_first_because: set captures the risen shape and prevents collapse

workflow.objective: confirm doneness by temperature and corroborating tests
workflow.do_first_because: objective doneness gates the pull decision

workflow.objective: enforce the safe internal temperature floor for egg/dairy
workflow.do_first_because: food safety cannot be traded for texture and gates release

workflow.objective: choose the pull point so carryover finishes set without drying
workflow.do_first_because: the pull point sets final moisture and set together

workflow.objective: diagnose any overflow, sinking, peaking, or cracking and correct levers
acceptance_tests: each defect mapped to a cause and fix
workflow.do_first_because: defects must be traced to levers before the next batch

workflow.objective: tune rack and convection for even domes across the pan
workflow.do_first_because: even heat placement prevents repeat defects

workflow.objective: lock the bake endpoint balancing moistness and structural set
workflow.do_first_because: a locked endpoint makes the whole bake reproducible

priority_rationale.notes: set locks the risen shape and prevents collapse
foundational; true temperature gates spring, set, and doneness
safety floor overrides all texture goals

dominance_rules.trigger: a texture preference for an underbaked egg/dairy center
dominance_rules.rule: food safety dominates; egg/dairy batter must reach the safe internal set temperature regardless of texture goals
dominance_rules.required_action: continue baking until the safe internal temperature is reached
dominance_rules.example: a gooey center is not served raw

dominance_rules.trigger: crumb not fully gelatinized but moisture goal urges an early pull
dominance_rules.rule: full gelatinization dominates over residual moisture; set first then preserve moisture
dominance_rules.required_action: bake to set then minimize over-bake
override_requires: documented intentional fudgy style with safe egg handling
dominance_rules.example: a gummy center is not accepted for moisture

dominance_rules.trigger: overflow appears when filling higher for dome height
dominance_rules.rule: the fill cap dominates; gain height from spring not overfill
dominance_rules.required_action: reduce fill to the dome band
dominance_rules.example: filling to the rim spills and is rejected

dominance_rules.trigger: peaking or cracking from a hotter oven used to bake faster
dominance_rules.rule: even-set quality dominates over speed; hold true temperature
dominance_rules.example: a hot fast oven peaks tops and is corrected

dominance_rules.trigger: a bone-dry toothpick target conflicts with crumb moisture after temp confirms set
dominance_rules.rule: once internal temperature confirms set, moisture preservation dominates over a drier pick
dominance_rules.required_action: accept moist crumbs on the pick and pull
override_requires: recipe needs a drier crumb by design
dominance_rules.example: chasing a dry pick over-dries cupcakes

dominance_rules.trigger: flat or sunken tops when extra sugar/fat is added for tenderness
dominance_rules.rule: rise-supporting structure dominates when the dome fails; cap tenderizers
dominance_rules.required_action: restore the viscosity floor before adding tenderizers
dominance_rules.example: too much sugar flattens the dome

dominance_rules.trigger: weak or uneven rise from rushing preheat or crowding pans
dominance_rules.rule: bake quality dominates over time saved; fully preheat and space pans
dominance_rules.example: a cold-start bake flattens the rise

dominance_rules.trigger: a measured doneness reading conflicts with a visual or timer judgment
dominance_rules.rule: calibrated internal temperature dominates over look or timer for the doneness call
dominance_rules.required_action: trust the calibrated probe and re-probe if needed
dominance_rules.example: a clean pick over a 90C core is treated as underdone

dominance_rules.trigger: an under-set moist crumb that stales or turns gummy fast
dominance_rules.rule: full set for shelf stability dominates over maximal fresh moisture when hold time matters
dominance_rules.required_action: set fully then preserve moisture within set
dominance_rules.example: an under-set moist crumb sours quickly

anti_rework_rules.rule: calibrate the oven before tuning any rise or doneness behavior
anti_rework_rules.rationale: every rise and set outcome depends on true temperature
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: chasing defects without knowing true temperature
anti_rework_rules.example: adjusting recipes to fix a hidden 15C offset

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix batter viscosity and fill before adjusting oven levers for doming
anti_rework_rules.rationale: viscosity and fill govern doming before heat
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: raising temperature to fix a flat thin batter
anti_rework_rules.example: cranking heat instead of thickening the batter

anti_rework_rules.rule: confirm structural set before making a doneness call
anti_rework_rules.rationale: doneness tests are meaningless before the crumb sets
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: calling done on a springy top over a raw core
anti_rework_rules.example: pulling on springback alone leaving a gummy center

anti_rework_rules.rule: clear the food safety floor before optimizing moisture or texture
anti_rework_rules.rationale: texture optimization must never undercut safety
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: tuning moisture below the safe set temperature
anti_rework_rules.example: leaving a center raw for fudginess

anti_rework_rules.rule: account for carryover before extending bake time for dryness
anti_rework_rules.rationale: residual heat finishes the bake and over-baking dries the crumb
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: baking bone-dry then drying further on the rack
anti_rework_rules.example: ignoring carryover and over-drying every batch

anti_rework_rules.rule: time leavener to the bake before blaming the oven for flat rise
anti_rework_rules.rationale: spent gas cannot be recovered by oven changes
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: raising temperature to fix an over-rested batter
anti_rework_rules.example: reheating to lift a batter whose gas is gone

anti_rework_rules.rule: diagnose defect root cause before changing multiple levers at once
anti_rework_rules.rationale: changing many levers blind hides the real cause
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: altering temp, fill, and leavener together without diagnosis
anti_rework_rules.example: shotgun fixes that mask the true sinking cause

anti_rework_rules.rule: map oven zones before choosing rack and convection settings
anti_rework_rules.rationale: placement decisions depend on the zone map
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: picking a rack without knowing hot and cold zones
anti_rework_rules.example: baking on a low rack over a hidden hot bottom

anti_rework_rules.rule: verify probe placement before acting on an internal temperature reading
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an air-pocket reading misleads the pull decision
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: acting on a single low reading from a cell
anti_rework_rules.example: overbaking after a false low probe in an air pocket
